title: Ridgeview reading roundup
content:
Context / why I wrote this:
Quick dump from the Ridgeview inference retreat (day 2 morning): focused on hallucination under RAG, KV-cache compression, and low-bit stability for long-context workloads. This is a rough, mixed bag: paper synopses, hypotheses we might test, links and quick commands. Mostly for me + Asha to pick up later.

Top-level takeaways (one-liners):
- Hallucination in RAG still often correlates with retrieval freshness + prompt framing; concise provenance injection reduces confident hallucinations more than heavy reranking in many small-scale tests.
- KV-cache compression (sparse + quantized shards) buys memory but introduces subtle token drift after long rollouts — need checks on population drift.
- 4-bit quant + per-head scale looks promising for throughput but some attention patterns break on reasoning chains longer than ~1.5k steps.

Papers + posts skimmed (quick notes):
1) "Anchored Retrieval for Factuality" (workshop paper):
- Idea: inject a short anchor token sequence before model input that enumerates provenance sentences and a simple 'trust score' token.
- Empirical: small reductions (10-20%) in factual hallucinations on closed-domain QA after anchor tuning.
- My note: anchor feels like a light-weight teacher signal — cheap to generate from top-k contexts. Try adding to our RAG pipeline as a feature toggle.

2) "Sparse-KV: Sharded Compression for KV Cache" (systems paper):
- Technique: partition KV by token-cluster (embedding cluster), compress each shard with distinct quant profile, store low-frequency shards on slower storage.
- Performance: 2.8x memory reduction for long-context Llama-variant; decode latency increase depends on eviction pattern.
- My note: matches our idea of hybrid DRAM/PMEM strategy. Watch out for mismatch between clustering at indexing time vs runtime token distribution.

3) "Per-Head 4-bit Quantization w/ Headwise Scales" (blog + code repo):
- Practical: scales per-head ranges and uses a small per-head residual table. Good fidelity on generation perplexity for many transforms.
- Caveat: some attention heads that gate positional patterns lose dynamic range and produce subtle repeat or omission errors on longer chains.

4) Conference talk: "Human-in-the-loop hallucination triage" (panel):
- Ops note: triage by high-confidence hallucination + low provenance overlap. Human labelers give 3x better ROI if they see the compact anchor snippets vs whole doc.

Ideas to try (experiments we can queue in ridgeview-experiments repo):
- Experiment A: Anchor injections in RAG
  - Pipeline: top-k retrieval (k=8) -> generate anchors (3 sentences max) -> prepend anchors + trust token -> model inference.
  - Metrics: hallucination rate on TruthQA subset, calibration (ECE), mean confidence on hallucinated outputs.
  - Hypothesis: anchors reduce confident hallucinations more than reranking.
  - Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ridgeview-experiments/pull/42 (starter branch).

- Experiment B: Sharded KV + selective eviction profiling
  - Setup: run long-context generation traces from sampled production sessions (we have traces in S3: s3://ridgeview-traces/2024-10/).
  - Variant 1: cluster-by-embedding -> shard -> compress 8-bit
  - Variant 2: cluster-by-frequency -> hot shards in DRAM, cold in PMEM
  - Metric: token drift (semantic similarity vs baseline) after 50k tokens, decode latency percentile (p50/p95).

- Experiment C: 4-bit per-head quant fidelity on reasoning chains
  - Inputs: chain-of-thought style prompts (math proofs, step-by-step).
  - Variation: apply per-head scaling only to FFN vs only to attention weights vs both.
  - Metric: correctness on GSM8K-ish subset, repetition/omission errors.

Open questions / hypotheses (brainstorm):
- Is 'anchor' effectiveness primarily prompting the model to check provenance, or does it change the latent distribution in a way that's orthogonal to retrieval quality? (Design: ablate anchor semantics vs random anchor text.)
- For KV-shards: does cluster drift over time cause catastrophic mismatch? If so, can we keep a small adaptive map (LRU-ish) to reassign tokens to shards on-the-fly?
- Per-head quant: can we detect which heads are 'positional' vs 'content' and protect them with higher bits dynamically? Could be a useful heuristic for mixed-bit execution.

Quick notes on evaluation design (do not overfit):
- Use a suite: fact-checking (closed-domain), open-domain QA (wikipedia), and production prompt traces (anonymized).
- Keep probes short and include calibration checks: ECE, CI for hallucination labels.
- Track latency budget impact (0.5–2.0 ms p50 acceptable for background async tasks; p95 tight).

Ops / infra notes (practicalities):
- For sharded KV we need provenance for re-compute cost. Make sure shard metadata includes creation-timestamp + approximate frequency counters.
- Add instrumentation in SDK to tag outputs that used anchors vs not, so we can slice metrics later.

Quick commands / notes for Asha / Devin to run locally:
- Pull the ridgeview-experiments branch: git checkout suhas/anchor-try; run `./run_rag_anchor.sh --k 8 --model ridge-13b-q4`
- KV trace location: aws s3 cp --recursive s3://ridgeview-traces/2024-10 ./traces/ --profile ridgeplay

Action items (short):
- [ ] Asha: spin up anchor ablation A/B on 1k eval samples (due 2034-11-20)
- [ ] Devin: prototype shard metadata + adaptive LRU map (due 2034-11-24)
- [ ] Me (Suhas): write short experiment brief and PR description (linked) and add evaluation metrics to the dashboard.

Loose thought-logs / random fragments (notes-to-self):
- If anchor helps mostly with confidence, maybe a cheaper approach is to post-process logits to lower confidence on unsupported facts instead of heavy re-ranking. Could be a band-aid.
- For long traces, maybe we only compress KV for tokens older than a threshold (e.g., t>3k) and leave the last 512 tokens unquantized. Simpler than weird clustering.
- Consider synthetic anchor generation: use light-weight QA model to summarize top-k as 1–2 anchor sentences.

References / bookmarks (copied here for convenience):
- Sparse-KV paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/xxxx.xxxxx
- Per-head quant blog: https://engineering.example.com/per-head-quant
- Workshop slides: https://slideshare.net/ridgeview/hallucination-anchor

Footer note: messy, intentionally. Keep this in users/ so we can iterate. Will move to shared_drives/engineering/ if we promote experiment to active sprint.

-- Suhas
